title: Agent: new SDK player (tool runner + structured outputs)
description: The new player implementing the Player interface (get_orders(game) -> list[Order]) on the raw Anthropic SDK. Per turn: one short-lived conversation via client.beta.messages.tool_runner with @beta_tool functions (validate_orders, route/distance queries) closing over game state; thinking={'type':'adaptive'}; cached rules system prompt (cache_control ephemeral) with plan+timeline+state in the user message after the breakpoint; final orders + updated plan extracted via structured outputs (messages.parse with a Pydantic TurnOrders model) instead of regex. Develop against claude-opus-4-8, then evaluate sonnet-5/haiku-4-5 as cheap opponents. Wire into existing decision/strategic loggers.

title: Agent: persistent plan object across turns
description: Small plan/scratchpad data structure the agent carries between turns: current strategy, acknowledged threats, and intents with expiry turns. Injected at the top of each turn's observation ('Your plan from last turn: ... update or continue it') and updated as part of the agent's structured output. Serialized alongside the game so runs can be replayed and plan drift inspected. This fixes the per-turn amnesia that made countdown reasoning impossible.

title: Engine: turn projection / timeline module
description: Pure, deterministic function in src/engine/ that computes the temporal picture for turns T..T+K: scheduled fleet arrivals (own + known enemy), per-star production, projected garrisons, defense deficits, and viable reinforcement options (which stars can send ships that arrive in time). This moves the temporal join out of the LLM and into tested game code — the LLM reads a schedule instead of simulating one. Fully unit-testable without any LLM. Output feeds the per-turn observation and the order-validation guardrail.

title: Fix ReactPlayer baseline bugs (trim + order extraction)
description: Two mechanical bugs in src/agent/react_player.py that corrupt the baseline before comparison runs: (1) trim_messages uses token_counter=len with max_tokens=8000, so the limit is effectively 8000 messages and only MAX_MESSAGES=20 triggers; when it does, strategy='last' can drop the initial game-state HumanMessage mid-turn, leaving the agent to issue orders blind. (2) Order extraction regex \[[\s\S]*?\] grabs the first bracketed span in the final message, which can capture prose/reasoning JSON instead of orders. Fix both so the old-vs-new agent comparison measures strategy, not harness failures.

title: Spec: new agent layer on Anthropic SDK
description: Design doc for the LangChain-free agent rewrite: module layout, data shapes for the persistent plan object and engine-computed timeline, per-turn request structure (cached rules system prompt + plan + timeline + state), and migration/retirement path for the five existing players (tools.py player, ReactPlayer, LangGraphPlayer, GraphReactPlayer, PythonReactAgent).

title: Retire old players and remove LangChain dependencies
description: Once the new player beats or matches baseline: delete the five old player implementations (tools.py player, ReactPlayer, LangGraphPlayer, GraphReactPlayer, PythonReactAgent), their tools/prompts/middleware modules, and associated tests; drop langchain, langchain-core, langchain-community, langchain-aws, langchain-openai, langchain-anthropic, langchain-ollama, and langgraph from pyproject.toml; point game.py and the server at the new player. uv sync + full test run to verify.

title: Eval: new agent vs ReactPlayer baseline runs
description: LLM-vs-LLM comparison games between the new SDK player and the fixed ReactPlayer baseline, using the existing analysis tooling (strategic_metrics, decision_logger, game_analyzer). Verify the temporal-reasoning failure mode is actually fixed: does the agent hold defensive commitments across turns, ignore too-late reinforcements, and coordinate arrival turns? Also sweep models (opus-4-8 vs sonnet-5 vs haiku-4-5) for the cost/quality curve.

title: Provider factory: Anthropic first-party + Bedrock Mantle
description: Replace llm_factory.py's LangChain multi-provider setup with a thin factory returning an Anthropic SDK client: anthropic.Anthropic() for first-party, AnthropicBedrockMantle(aws_region=...) for Bedrock (model IDs get the 'anthropic.' prefix there). Same messages/tool_runner surface either way. OpenAI/Ollama paths are dropped; old players remain available if those comparisons are ever wanted.

title: Guardrail: validate_orders rejects timeline-contradicting orders
description: Extend order validation from advice to enforcement: reject orders that contradict the computed timeline (e.g., stripping the home garrison below the projected deficit while a known threat arrives within K turns) and bounce them back to the agent with the specific violation so it can revise.

title: Prompt: minimal rules prompt replacing 600-line doctrine
description: Rewrite the system prompt down to: game rules, output contract, and 'here is the computed analysis — choose and revise your plan'. Most of the current prompt (timing doctrine, combat-calculation walkthroughs, REPL examples) exists to teach the model computations the timeline module now does deterministically. Frozen/stable so it can carry a prompt-cache breakpoint.

title: Update CLAUDE.md agent-delegation guidance post-LangChain
description: CLAUDE.md routes LLM/agent coding to the langchain-agent-architect subagent, which no longer makes sense once the agent layer is on the raw Anthropic SDK. Update the delegation rule (and consider a new/renamed subagent definition in .claude/agents/) to match the SDK-based stack.
